paper_metadata.title: Structure and properties of metastable Ti–Nb–Sn–Mo alloys

evidence.quote: In this study, novel metastable Ti–(9–13)Nb–7Sn–(2–6)Mo alloys were developed using Bo–Md method.
Ti–Nb-based alloys have been widely developed for bio-medical applications due to their low elastic modulus.
Six new metastable Ti–Nb–Sn–Mo alloys were developed by adding Mo element to the Ti–25Nb–8Sn alloy
Ti–25Nb–8Sn
including Ti–9Nb–7Sn–4Mo, Ti–9Nb–7Sn–6Mo, Ti–11Nb–7Sn–3Mo, Ti–11Nb–7Sn–5Mo, Ti–13Nb–7Sn–2Mo, and Ti–13Nb–7Sn–4Mo.

The quaternary Ti–Nb–Sn–Mo alloys were designed for this study, including Ti–9Nb–7Sn–4Mo, Ti–9Nb–7Sn–6Mo, Ti–11Nb–7Sn–3Mo, Ti–11Nb–7Sn–5Mo, Ti–13Nb–7Sn–2Mo, and Ti–13Nb–7Sn–4Mo. The Ti–Nb–Sn–Mo alloys were prepared with a commercial arc-melting vacuum pressure cast-ing system (A-028, DAWN SHINE, Taiwan) by using Ti (99.7 wt% pure), Nb (99.95 wt% pure), Sn (99.9 wt% pure), and Mo (99.95 wt% pure).

evidence.quote: The Ti–Nb–Sn–Mo alloys were prepared with a commercial arc-melting vacuum pressure cast-ing system (A-028, DAWN SHINE, Taiwan) by using Ti (99.7 wt% pure), Nb (99.95 wt% pure), Sn (99.9 wt% pure), and Mo (99.95 wt% pure). All the Ti alloy ingots were melted more than five times for homogenizing the constituent elements.

The surfaces of all alloys were mechanically polished according to a standard metallographic procedure to a final level of 0.06 μm SiO2 polishing suspension. After cleaning the surface of the samples with deionized water, the samples were soaked in alcohol and cleaned using an ultrasonic cleaner. XRD and three-point bending tests were performed on the polished alloys.

All the quaternary Ti alloys showed a dendritic structure, which is a typical microstructural feature of as-cast alloy.
the equiaxed β grains were observed in the metallographic photos of the β -phase Ti–Nb–Sn–Mo alloys.
A small amount of fine needle-like α" phase was also observed in the dual-phase (α " + β) Ti–Nb–Sn–Mo alloys.
Ti–Nb–Sn–Mo alloys had high bending strength (1145–1255 MPa).
Also, Ti–Nb–Sn–Mo alloys presented low elastic modulus (53–63 GPa).

Furthermore, the moduli of resilience of Ti–Nb–Sn–Mo alloys were as high as 4.05–7.99 MJ/m3, which is significantly higher than those of commercially pure Ti (1.16 MJ/m 3) and Ti–25Nb–8Sn (3.02 MJ/m3).
